proposed_comments.title: Read the Robocopy UI module settings file

confidence.rationale: At the pinned head GetSettings<T> defaults its module argument to an empty string, but module settings are stored by module name; the literal module-aware replacement is compiled in the exact-head candidate.

proposed_comments.body:
### Read the Robocopy UI module settings file

**Severity:** `high`

`GetSettings<RobocopyUISettings>()` uses the default settings overload, whose module name defaults to an empty string. The `UseLegacySaveMode` setting belongs to the Robocopy UI module, so this reads the root settings file instead and can ignore the value configured for `.rcj` saves. Pass `RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName` to the module-aware settings accessor.

```suggestion
        if (SettingsUtils.Default.GetSettingsOrDefault<RobocopyUISettings>(RobocopyUISettings.ModuleName).Properties.UseLegacySaveMode.Value)
```

proposed_comments.title: Gate the launch waiter on the module lifecycle

confidence.rationale: The pinned constructor starts the event waiter unconditionally, disable only clears _enabled, the callback ignores wait errors, and StartProcess/IsProcessActive access the process handle without synchronization.

proposed_comments.body:
### Gate the launch waiter on the module lifecycle

**Severity:** `high`

The constructor starts a global named-event waiter unconditionally, but `disable()` only clears `_enabled` and `StartProcess()` does not check it. A signal can therefore launch Robocopy UI while the module is disabled; the callback also ignores wait failures, and concurrent event/custom-action launches can race while checking and storing `m_process`. Start the waiter during `enable()`, stop it during `disable()`, return on unsuccessful wait results, and synchronize access to the tracked process handle across launch and shutdown.
